newsitem.title: FINLAND: LIPPONEN CALLS FOR UNITY BEHIND PRO-EMU STANCE.
newsitem.headline: LIPPONEN CALLS FOR UNITY BEHIND PRO-EMU STANCE.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said at the weekend that all parties in the left-right-green coalition should support the official government target that Finland be in the first group to join Europe's single currency.
"The prime minister demands a joint government EMU stance," daily Turun Sanomat said on Sunday, referring to an interview with Lipponen.
He also said the government parties' parliamentary groups, controlling 141 seats in the 200-strong legislature, should stand united behind the pro-EMU membership proposal.
"I can not see the EMU decision being made while parliament is in a state of jamboree," Lipponen said.

Of the five cabinet parties, only the conservatives are not openly split on Finnish membership of the third stage of economic and monetary union, scheduled for start-up in 1999. The Leftist Alliance will arrange a vote among party members.
The government has said it will give to parliament a notification regarding its plans to see Finland join EMU in the first group.

Parliament is due to vote early next year for or against the proposal. According to the government's plan, the EMU vote will also be a vote of confidence in the coalition, whose four-year term runs until March 1999. -- Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 240, news@reuters.fi
